To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) pollination success was significantly greater on organic farms than on conventional farms, and that this difference was already present 2-4 years after conversion; (2) organic farming was positively correlated with the number of pollinators, but negatively correlated with the proportion of pollinators visiting strawberry plants.
pollination success in strawberry plants was higher on organic compared conventional farms and this effect was already evident 4 years after conversion.
pollination success of strawberries is higher on organic compared with conventional farms, and this is already evident 2-4 years after conversion.

the effects of organic farming on the pollination of strawberry, a crop that is heavily dependent on insect pollinators.
how the conversion to organic farming affects pollination success in strawberry.
the effect of organic and conventional farming practices on pollination success of strawberry plants and how this relates to pollinator abundance.

organic farming can be a good way to increase pollination success in strawberry, but more research is needed to confirm these results.
